Type rules prefer inference, ban implicit any, use Record<PropertyKey, unknown> over object, favor interface for object shapes and type for unions, and rank @ts-expect-error above @ts-ignore above as any. Module augmentation via declare module replaces namespace patterns; extensibility exposes small mergeable interfaces at source types. Structure favors named exports over default except where Next.js or React.lazy require defaults, object destructuring, and reusing helpers from packages/utils before duplicating locally. UI guidance mandates @lobehub/ui and Ant Design over raw HTML, antd-style tokens for theming, dark mode and mobile responsiveness. Performance limits DB column selection; logging avoids debug package and never logs secrets.

items.name: system-design

items.description: Turn vague scale goals into requirements-first designs using load balancers, caches, queues, and sizing estimates before you commit to architecture.
items.summary: System Design is an agent skill presenting a structured framework for large-scale distributed architecture and interview-style designs. Core principle: start with requirements, not solutions, assembling load balancers, caches, queues, databases, and CDNs with explicit tradeoffs. A 0-10 scoring rubric expects stated requirements, estimates, building blocks, scaling, reliability, and acknowledged compromises. The four-step process spends five to ten minutes on scope, fifteen to twenty on a high-level diagram, fifteen to twenty on critical components, and five on tradeoffs. Back-of-envelope estimation covers powers of two, latency numbers, availability nines, QPS from DAU, and storage from record size times retention. Building blocks detail L4 versus L7 load balancers, cache strategies, Kafka or SQS decoupling, and consistent hashing. Database scaling contrasts SQL versus NoSQL, replication, and sharding with hotspot mitigation. Common designs include URL shorteners, rate limiters, news feeds, chat, and Snowflake IDs. Reliability covers health checks, observability pillars, blue-green and canary deploys, RPO and RTO, and autoscaling signals.
